query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a modest Al addition (~5 at%) into equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will form a stable, protective alumina scale in air at elevated temperatures, reducing oxygen ingress and thus enhancing oxidation resistance compared to the undoped alloy, while minimally affecting the alloy’s high-temperature strength or room-temperature ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr in the as-cast condition with 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility and yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C (strain rate: 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1).
generation.intervention: Alloying HfNbTaTiZr with ~5 atomic percent aluminum.
generation.conditions: Expose the Al-doped alloy in air at 800 °C for up to 5 hours while maintaining a tensile load equivalent to the service stress of the baseline alloy at these conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: An adherent α-Al₂O₃ layer forms on the alloy surface, suppressing internal oxidation and pesting reactions.
generation.mechanism: The added Al partitions to the surface under oxidation, creating an alumina scale with low oxygen diffusion, thereby reducing oxidation kinetics and oxygen embrittlement in the bulk.
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduced scale growth rate and oxide spallation, leading to significantly improved oxidation resistance, with minimal decline of mechanical properties compared to the undoped alloy in the specified temperature and strain-rate regime.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, which exhibits poor oxygen resistance in air at elevated temperatures and suffers from oxidatively induced embrittlement or “pesting.”
generation.boundary: Effect is expected to hold for exposure temperatures up to ~800 °C in air for short-to-intermediate durations (≤5 hours) under moderate tensile loading. Longer or higher-temperature exposures may require additional protective measures or higher Al contents, with potential trade-offs in mechanical properties.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of ductility retention and oxidation resistance improvement at temperatures above 800 °C or for exposure times longer than 5 hours remains unverified without direct empirical data.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two sets of samples: (1) undoped equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr (control) and (2) the same alloy with ~5 at% Al. Expose both sets to air at 800 °C for 5 hours under a standardized tensile load. Measure oxide scale thickness, oxygen ingress, mass change, tensile ductility, and yield strength before and after exposure.
measurements: Scale thickness and spallation by cross-sectional microscopy
Mechanical properties (yield strength and ductility) post-exposure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the Al-containing alloy does not form a more protective alumina scale (i.e., exhibits similar or greater mass gain or oxide spallation as the undoped alloy at 800 °C), or if the mechanical properties degrade similarly or more severely than the undoped alloy after exposure under identical conditions.
